text: Large Language Models, or LLMs, are computer programs that can understand and produce human language. They work by predicting the next word in a sentence, based on patterns learned from huge amounts of text. This training data includes books, websites and articles, which helps the model learn grammar, facts and common ways of writing. Users can improve results through prompt engineering, which means writing clear and specific instructions. LLMs are good at tasks like summarizing, translating and answering questions. However, they also have limits: they can make mistakes, give outdated information, or produce false details that sound convincing. Therefore, it is always wise to check important answers yourself.
